answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the only record showing a concrete, quantified cost reduction via a low-cost vendor, and it claims quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — both directly relevant to the 14-day window and the constraint of not adding delivery risk. Because finance demands an 18% cut and the incumbent has flatly refused to reopen price, renew_incumbent (memory_c1, memory_c6) cannot satisfy the cost mandate; negotiate_terms (memory_c4) is likewise blocked this cycle since the incumbent has already said no. Deferring (memory_c5) would leave the assembly line with no contract in 14 days and no buffer, creating unacceptable delivery risk. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses resilience but not cost. Switching to the validated low-cost vendor is the one action that attacks cost while the onboarding track record suggests delivery risk is manageable. Verification of memory_c2 is needed because the decision hinges entirely on the accuracy of that onboarding and invoicing record.
